85.0.0.en: 1- Lord, thou hast been favourable unto thy land: thou hast brought back the captivity of Jacob.

85.0.1.en: 1- After the people of God tasted the humiliation of bondage in captivity, they repented and returned to God, so God was pleased with them, and consequently was pleased with the land He had given to His people, the land of Canaan, for they had defiled it with their sins, and the Assyrians and Babylonians destroyed it. But it was sanctified by the repentance of His people and by His consequent pleasure in their land. The writer of the Psalm says “thy land” because God is the Creator of the earth and of the whole world, and He is also the Giver of the land of Canaan to His people, and it was He who sanctified it by the presence of His temple in it.

85.0.2.en: 2- The Psalm thanks God, who began to bring His people back from captivity at the hand of Zerubbabel, which was the first return. It thanks Him for gathering His people from the dispersion and bringing them back by the authority of the king himself, to dwell in their land and to build the temple of God. The Psalm says “the captivity of Jacob” and not Israel, because Jacob was the righteous one, of whom the Scripture bore witness that he was a perfect man dwelling in tents (Gen 25:27). Then God blessed him by the hand of Isaac and appeared to him on the ladder reaching up to heaven, then spoke to him many times, and appeared to him afterward at Penuel, and rescued him from the hand of Esau. He is beloved by God, and therefore his offspring return to the land that was promised to Jacob, that is, God brings back the captivity of Jacob.

85.0.3.en: 3- This verse is a prophecy of God's good pleasure in the world, and of His redemption by the Cross so that His children who believe in Him might return from the captivity of Satan after He bound him.

85.1.0.en: 2- Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people, thou hast covered all their sin. Selah.

85.1.1.en: 1- When the people of God repented in captivity, God forgave them all their iniquities and sins, for God longs for His people to return to Him. He covered all their evil deeds and blotted them out, so that they did not appear to men, for He is a compassionate God who desires not only the salvation of His people but also to glorify them before the rest of the peoples, while hiding their sins.

85.1.2.en: 2- Although God forgave His captive people, it was in the hope of their redemption by the Cross, so the forgiveness was not completed except by Christ, who forgave and covered, and still covers and forgives the sins of His people when they repent.

85.1.3.en: 3- The word “Selah” is a musical pause for meditating on the mercies of God and His forgiveness.

85.2.0.en: 3- Thou hast taken away all thy wrath: thou hast turned thyself from the fierceness of thine anger.

85.2.1.en: God is holy and just, and He is repelled by and angry at any sin. Repentance stops the wrath of God and looses all the bonds of indignation, which is the intense anger, so that man enjoys the peace of God, His love and His care. This is what happened to the repentant captives, and it was completed by the redemption of Christ.

85.2.2.en: How great you are, O repentance, you who break all the shackles of sin and release those who believe in you into the new life with God, so that they enjoy His fellowship. Therefore, O my soul, do not let repentance leave you all your life, every day and every hour, for it is your helper and it opens the arms of God.

85.3.s.en: (2) Asking for the mercies of God

85.3.0.en: 4- Turn us, O God of our salvation, and cause thine anger toward us to cease. 5- Wilt thou be angry with us for ever? wilt thou draw out thine anger to all generations?

85.3.1.en: “Cause to cease” (anf): make it banished, that is, put it far away.

85.3.2.en: 1- The fatherly feelings of the writer of the Psalm appear, for he rejoiced in God's mercy in the return of some of the people, and he asks God to forgive the rest, that is, to move them to repentance, and to forgive them and bring them back to Him, and consequently His anger is lifted from them, for God is merciful and does not wish His anger to last from generation to generation and for ever.

85.3.3.en: 2- If God's anger, which appears in disciplining His people with afflictions such as captivity, is a very heavy matter, how much more severe must His anger be in eternal torment! Therefore today we cry out with all our hearts that God may accept our repentance and lift His anger from us, so that we may return to our sonship to Him and enjoy His care.

85.4.0.en: 6- Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee? 7- Shew us thy mercy, O Lord, and grant us thy salvation.

85.4.1.en: After God lifts His anger and accepts the repentance of His people, He gives them life with Him, which is true happiness and joy. This is the divine salvation and mercy, which was completed in Christ the Redeemer, who raised us to fellowship with Him and to joy in Him on earth, after He removed our sins from us by His blood, that we might enjoy the earnest of the heavenly Kingdom. This salvation and this mercy are what we receive today through the Holy Sacraments in the Church of the New Testament.

85.4.2.en: 1- David prayed for his enemies, but his prayer returned to his bosom, that is, God rejoiced in David's prayer and blessed him with good, but did not answer his prayer, because of the evil of his enemies.

85.4.3.en: 2- The return of the prayer to David's bosom moved his heart to pray again, and thus he lived in what is called constant prayer, so that he said of himself, “but I give myself unto prayer” (Ps 109:4).

85.4.4.en: 3- Christ prayed for those who crucified Him while He was on the Cross, that God might forgive them, but they did not benefit, because of their insistence on evil and their unbelief.

85.4.5.en: Enjoy true joy in being with God in prayer and meditation, for life is in Christ, while the joys of the world are vain and passing. And abide in His Church and its Sacraments, and you will live in salvation for ever.

85.5.s.en: (3) Hope in the mercies of God

85.5.0.en: 8- I will hear what God the Lord will speak: for he will speak peace unto his people, and to his saints: but let them not turn again to folly.

85.5.1.en: 1- The writer of the Psalm hears the voice of God through the prophets who speak to the people, especially to those among them who fear God, so that they may remain firm in faith and in the fear of God and not return to the foolishness of sin and to conduct that turns away from God in the worship of idols, or any evil conduct. The condition for hearing the voice of God and benefiting from it is the fear of God, which keeps man away from sin.

85.5.2.en: 2- The voice of God is Christ, who became incarnate in the fullness of time to proclaim salvation to all mankind, especially to those who fear God, whether Jews or Gentiles, so that they believe in Him and do not return to the folly of sin.

85.6.0.en: 9- Surely his salvation is nigh them that fear him; that glory may dwell in our land.

85.6.1.en: 1- Whoever fears God keeps His commandments, therefore God draws near to him and grants him His salvation, that is, saves him from his sins and pours His blessings upon him, and even is glorified in him, and this glory dwells and settles in the children of God, because it is manifest in their works and in their lives, which glorify God.

85.6.2.en: 2- Salvation is accomplished by Christ, and it is near to those who fear God and await the expected Messiah. The writer of the Psalm saw, in the spirit of prophecy, that the Incarnation of Christ had become near, and that He would come and give salvation to those who fear the Lord, and thus glory dwells in our land through the Incarnation of Christ upon it.

85.7.0.en: 10- Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.

85.7.1.en: 1- In Christ Jesus mercy and truth, which is justice, were fulfilled. For truth requires the death of the sinner, and mercy requires that death be lifted from him. So Christ died and rose from the dead, to remove our sins from us, and that we might receive mercy in Him.

85.7.2.en: 2- Likewise in Christ righteousness and peace kissed each other, that is, each accepted the other and they were united, and Christ even gave them to everyone who believes in Him. So the believer has peace, and an inclination toward righteousness, that is, toward doing good and what is right.

85.8.0.en: 11- Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven.

85.8.1.en: 1- The Truth is Christ, who springs out of the earth by His Incarnation. And Christ is God who came down from heaven, or He is the righteousness that dawned on us from heaven. So the One who is on earth is at the same time the One who is from heaven.

85.8.2.en: 2- Our faith in the Truth, who is Christ, springs up within us, that is, we live the faith in Christ, and then righteousness looks down on us, that is, by faith we are able to live righteousness and to live as heavenly beings on earth, walking in the Spirit and adorning ourselves with virtues.

85.9.0.en: 12- Yea, the Lord shall give that which is good; and our land shall yield her increase.

85.9.1.en: God is the Giver of good to His children, that is, He gives them the inclination to do good, for God renews the nature of His children in the Sacrament of Baptism, so that it has an inclination to become like God, to keep His commandments, and to serve others. And thus the good increase of the land appears, that is, the spiritual fruits; that is, unless God gives the inclination to do good we cannot bear spiritual fruits. And God gives all people this gift and waits for our response to Him.

85.10.0.en: 13- Righteousness shall go before him; and shall tread in the way of his steps.

85.10.1.en: 1- Righteousness here is repentance, which goes before Christ so that He may dwell in the hearts of His children. And by this He tramples every evil in the believing soul, and Christ dwells in the heart and fills it with peace and joy.

85.10.2.en: 2- Righteousness is also Christ, who walks before the Father and tramples sin and its consequence, which is death. By His death He trampled death on the Cross, and rose and ascended into the heavens, and opened the way for those who believe in Him, that they may enter heaven.

85.10.3.en: Repentance is your way to eternity, so live in it every day and you will receive the blessings of heaven and feel Christ in your life, and taste the sweetness of eternity while you are on earth, and live in a joy that lasts for ever. A prayer and thanksgiving. A prayer of David. “Bow down thine ear, O Lord, hear me ...” (v. 1). Introduction:

85.10.5.en: 2- When was it written? When David was pursued from the face of Saul, or from the face of Absalom his son.

85.10.6.en: 3- It suits the soul that needs God, or that is in distress but whose faith in Him is strong; this prayer supports it and gives it hope.

85.10.7.en: 4- This Psalm is liturgical, and it used to be chanted by the Levites and the people on the great Day of Atonement, which is a type of Good Friday.

85.10.8.en: 5- This Psalm is a comprehensive prayer, that is, it includes petition, repentance, thanksgiving and praise. It is many-sided, showing that David is a man of prayer, and encouraging everyone who loves prayer, as it covers the different aspects of his life.

85.10.9.en: 6- This Psalm is found in the prayer of the Sixth Hour, in which Christ was crucified, because it is full of prayers and supplications from a needy, repentant heart, looking to Christ the Redeemer to answer him, save him from his enemies, and gladden his heart. This Psalm also represents the prayers of the suffering Christ on the Cross, who by His death triumphed over Satan and bound him, and trampled death by His death.

86.0.0.en: 1- Bow down thine ear, O Lord, hear me: for I am poor and needy.

86.0.1.en: 1- David asks God to condescend and incline His ear, because He is the great God, exalted above all His creation. And David declares that he is poor and needy, because he is weak, a sinner, and driven out of Jerusalem. Consequently he does not enjoy the worship of God in His house, and he feels his need of God. Therefore he asks Him to listen to him and incline His ear, that is, to take interest in his prayer and answer him. This shows David's humility and his declaration of his great need.

86.0.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ, humble and suffering on the Cross, who declares before the Father that He took the form of poverty and misery for the redemption of mankind, and asks the Father, as a man, to condescend, to listen to Him and to answer Him.

86.1.0.en: 2- Preserve my soul; for I am holy: O thou my God, save thy servant that trusteth in thee.

86.1.1.en: 1- David declares that the reason for his godliness is his trust in God, and because he fears God and trusts in Him, he asks God to preserve him from the wicked who want to destroy him. At the same time he defends himself before the wicked who accuse him of evil and pursue him, so he says to God: I fear You and revere You, and I am not as they accuse me, and I am Your servant, submissive to You and trusting in You.

86.1.2.en: 2- This verse is also a prophecy about Christ the godly, or the righteous, who trusts in God, who took the form of a servant by His Incarnation, and asks the Father to preserve Him before the cruelty of the wicked who crucified Him, in order to confirm His humanity.

86.2.0.en: 3- Be merciful unto me, O Lord: for I cry unto thee all the day.

86.2.1.en: This verse shows the extent of David's suffering, for afflictions surrounded him all day long and for a long period, so he cried out to God asking for His mercy, for He was his only hope and the compassionate heart able to embrace him however great the evils of his enemies. Thus David continued to cry out to God for many years until prayer became habitual, and his whole life became prayer, and the responsibilities of kingship did not keep him from God. He was anointed king since he was a boy, and Saul pursued him, and then after he reigned Absalom drove him out; through all this he continued to cry out asking for the mercy of God.

86.3.0.en: 4- Rejoice the soul of thy servant: for unto thee, O Lord, do I lift up my soul.

86.3.1.en: David trusts in God not only to preserve him during the affliction but also to gladden his heart. And David strove and struggled by lifting his heart to God, that is, he rose above the preoccupations of the world, its desires and its cares, seeking the vision of God that gives him joy.

86.4.0.en: 5- For thou, Lord, art good, and ready to forgive; and plenteous in mercy unto all them that call upon thee.

86.4.1.en: David concludes this part of his prayer by showing the attributes of God that encouraged him to make the preceding petitions. These attributes are:

86.4.2.en: 1- That He is good, so He is not pleased with the evils directed against David.

86.4.3.en: 2- That He is forgiving, which encourages David to draw near to God, who is able to forgive his sins, and this shows David's confession that he is a sinner in need of forgiveness.

86.4.4.en: 3- That He is plenteous in mercy, so He cares for David the poor, driven out by the wicked and in need of the mercy of God.

86.4.5.en: The mercies of God encourage you to draw near to Him however great your sins, and however great your weakness, He cares for you, keeps you and protects you from every evil, and even gives you peace and gladdens your heart, so rejoice and do not hesitate, for He loves you.

86.5.0.en: 6- Give ear, O Lord, unto my prayer; and attend to the voice of my supplications.

86.5.1.en: David draws near to God with humility, asking Him to hear his prayer and his supplications. And out of his great need he says “give ear” and “attend,” because his sufferings are many, and he needs God to listen to them carefully and rescue him from them. It is clear that he prays many times, since he says “supplications,” because his sufferings are successive, but his hope in God is confident.

86.6.0.en: 7- In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee: for thou wilt answer me.

86.6.1.en: David experienced God's support in his life and was assured in taking refuge in Him, so when trouble comes upon him he calls on God quickly, and He answers him. He has learned and become accustomed to seek God in every trouble, and He rescues him from it.

86.7.0.en: 8- Among the gods there is none like unto thee, O Lord; neither are there any works like unto thy works.

86.7.1.en: God's intervention to rescue His children in the hour of trouble is a very powerful intervention, because He is God, able to do all things, and He is of course higher than all the pagan gods, who are demons. And His works are greater than any works, as He saved His people from the hand of Pharaoh of Egypt, and later from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria.

86.8.0.en: 9- All nations whom thou hast made shall come and worship before thee, O Lord; and shall glorify thy name.

86.8.1.en: 10- For thou art great, and doest wondrous things: thou art God alone.

86.8.2.en: The power of God manifested in His people before the rest of the peoples draws these peoples, that is, the Gentiles, to faith, and they declare their faith by coming to Jerusalem and worshiping God, who is great and does wondrous things. His greatest wonders are His Incarnation, His redemption and His Resurrection, in addition to His many miracles, which strengthen the faith of His people and of the Gentiles who believe in Him, and thus the Church is formed of the Jews and the victorious Gentiles.

86.8.3.en: If the works of God are mighty and wondrous, do not be troubled if any affliction or problems face you, for your God is able to do all things; He will rescue you and keep you, and even grant you a peace that surpasses all understanding.

86.9.0.en: 11- Teach me thy way, O Lord; I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name.

86.9.1.en: 1- David asks God to teach him His way. And the way is Christ, that is: give me, O God, Your knowledge, especially since God cannot be known without His support, and when I know You I will be able to walk in Your truth, which is to keep away from sin and to acquire purity of heart, and on the other hand to walk in the different virtues, which is the spiritual life as it is lived.

86.9.2.en: 2- David also asks God to unite his heart to fear Him, so that it is not a heart divided between the love of the world and the love of God, but his aim is the fear of God, so he rejects all evil, and then he is enlightened spiritually and enjoys fellowship with God.

86.10.0.en: 12- I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with all my heart: and I will glorify thy name for evermore.

86.10.1.en: When David's heart was united in the fear of God, his heart and all his feelings were released to praise God, and since he delighted in it on earth, he longed to remain in it for ever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

86.11.0.en: 13- For great is thy mercy toward me: and thou hast delivered my soul from the lowest hell.

86.11.1.en: David saw, in the spirit of prophecy, the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption, so he declared that God's mercy toward him is great, which he will receive in the fullness of time, when Christ will bring him up from the lowest hell, for Hades has degrees. So Christ delivers His children from all their sins, even if they were in the depths of Hades, that is, its hardest degrees.

86.11.2.en: Do not forget to thank God every day for His gifts, for this fills your heart with joy and increases your enjoyment of His gifts, in addition to the abundance of new gifts that God pours out upon you.

86.12.0.en: 14- O God, the proud are risen against me, and the assemblies of violent men have sought after my soul; and have not set thee before them.

86.12.1.en: 1- David's enemies rose up against him to destroy him, and because they left God they lost the fear of Him, and consequently it became easy for them to wrong others and even kill them, and therefore there was no chance of escape from their hands except by the power of God, for they were tyrants, proud, and persistent in evil.

86.12.2.en: 2- The Jews who rose up against Christ are the proud and the tyrants, who sought the help of the Roman authority and crucified Christ, because they did not fear God, so they killed Christ, but by His power He rose from the dead. The demons also do likewise in their wars against men, but God delivers His children and gives them victory over the demons.

86.13.0.en: 15- But thou, O Lord, art a God full of compassion, and gracious, longsuffering, and plenteous in mercy and truth.

86.13.1.en: If the demons and all the wicked who follow them are hard of heart and want to destroy the righteous, because the fear of God is not before them, then God intervenes with His mercy and compassion to protect His children, and even is longsuffering toward them however great their sins, and gives them an opportunity to repent, especially since He fulfilled truth and mercy in the Cross of Christ, for by His redemption He paid the debt of sin, and in His mercy offered salvation to His people.

86.14.0.en: 16- O turn unto me, and have mercy upon me; give thy strength unto thy servant, and save the son of thine handmaid.

86.14.1.en: 1- David asks God to look at him, have mercy on him, and rescue him from the hands of his enemies. And he asks with boldness because he is the servant of God, and the son of His handmaid, that is, one who belongs to Him and was born in His house, and consequently he can enjoy the care and protection of God.

86.14.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about the crucified Christ, who cried out while on the Cross, “My God, my God ...” (Mt 27:46), because He humbled Himself as a man and took the form of a servant, and He is the Son of the Virgin, the handmaid of God, that is, His female servant. He is Son by nature, not like the rest of mankind, who are children by adoption.

86.15.0.en: 17- Shew me a token for good; that they which hate me may see it, and be ashamed: because thou, Lord, hast holpen me, and comforted me.

86.15.1.en: 1- David asks God to work with him a good sign that those around him who hate him may see, so that they are ashamed and confounded, by rescuing David from their hands and glorifying him, and this is what actually happened. And it was repeated with Christ, to whom the Father turned, and in whom the greatest sign in the world appeared, which is His Resurrection from the dead, and the demons were put to shame.

86.15.2.en: 2- Although the whole Psalm asks for God's mercy and help, David declares at the end of the Psalm, with faith and confidence, that God gave him great help and comforted his heart, and after this the grace of God to David was completed after the killing of Absalom, when David returned to his throne with great honor.

86.15.3.en: Ask with humility everything you want from God, and He will answer you, for He loves the humble and hastens to them, and rescues them from every evil.

86.15.4.en: Jerusalem, the city of salvation. By the sons of Korah. A Psalm, a song of praise. “His foundation is in the holy mountains ...” (v. 1). Introduction:

86.15.6.en: a- The sons of Korah, who did not take part in the rebellion of their father Korah, as we mentioned in the introduction to (Ps 84).

86.15.7.en: b- David the prophet, who gave it to the sons of Korah to chant.

86.15.9.en: a- In the days of King Hezekiah, when this king took care to restore the temple, especially since Babylon had begun to become famous in those days, and was even close to seizing the world and dominating it, and at that time Egypt was called Rahab, as Isaiah the prophet mentions (Isa 30:7).

86.15.10.en: b- In the days of David, when he brought the ark of the covenant of God back to Jerusalem and prepared the materials for building the temple that his son Solomon would build.

86.15.11.en: 3- This Psalm is considered one of the Messianic Psalms that speak to us clearly about the Incarnation of Christ.

86.15.12.en: 4- This Psalm is one of the “Songs of Zion” that glorify Jerusalem, the city of God, such as (Ps 48, Ps 76).

86.15.13.en: 5- This Psalm speaks clearly about the salvation of the Gentiles in Christ Jesus.

86.15.14.en: 6- This Psalm speaks not only about Jerusalem, but about the Church of the New Testament, and the heavenly Jerusalem.

86.15.15.en: 7- The Church chants this Psalm in the greatest of her prayers, the Divine Liturgy, in the days of the Great Fast, immediately before the absolution of the servants, and says it in the Coptic language, “Nef Sinti.”

86.15.16.en: 8- This Psalm is found in the prayer of the Sixth Hour, because in this hour Christ was crucified to save mankind, Jews and Gentiles, and so that the New Jerusalem, that is, the Church, might be open to receive everyone who believes from mankind.
